name: Undifferentiated Embryonal Sarcoma of the Liver

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for UESL

criteria.description: Presence of undifferentiated spindle and stellate tumor cells with abundant myxoid stroma on liver biopsy
Large, solitary hepatic mass with cystic and solid components on imaging (ultrasound, CT, MRI)
Positive staining for vimentin and variable expression of desmin and cytokeratin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of undifferentiated sarcoma cells combined with characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of other hepatic malignancies such as hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to liver tumor
searchTerms: abdominal swelling due to liver mass
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

rare.symptomName: Spontaneous tumor rupture with intra-abdominal hemorrhage

laboratory: Mild to moderate elevation of liver transaminases (AST, ALT)
Non-specific inflammatory markers elevated (e.g., ESR, CRP)
imaging: Large, heterogeneous hepatic mass with mixed cystic and solid areas on ultrasound
CT scan showing well-demarcated lesion with areas of necrosis and hemorrhage
MRI demonstrating high T2 signal intensity with internal septations
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; complex karyotypes reported in some cases
other: Histopathology showing undifferentiated spindle and stellate cells with myxoid matrix
Immunohistochemistry positive for vimentin, variable desmin and cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: Typically occurs in younger children under 5 years
Histology shows epithelial and mesenchymal elements
Usually occurs in older children or adults with underlying liver disease
Elevated AFP and liver function abnormalities
Occurs in infants and young children

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging abdominal mass in a child
Signs of tumor rupture or intra-abdominal hemorrhage
Unexplained persistent fever with hepatic mass
references: Stocker JT, Ishak KG. Undifferentiated (embryonal) sarcoma of the liver: report of 31 cases. Cancer. 1978.
Kelley RI, et al. Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver: clinical and pathologic features. J Pediatr Hematol Oncol. 2010.
Orphanet: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver. ORPHA:178315.
